Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-04-20
Comments: In order to prevent further spread of COVID-19, Commonwealth offices are currently closed until April 30. During this time period, this inspector is working remotely to continue the mission of the Pennsylvania Department of Environment Protection. This administrative inspection is being conducted to document violations at the site. On 04/15/2020 Kyle Borden of CNX reported a 5 barrel produced fluid release from a valve in a 3" produced water line servicing the GH 122 well. On 04/16/2020 I spoke to Kyle Borden via phone. Borden indicated the spill is approximately 50' before the pad on the east side of the access road. The leak occurred in a 3” poly line valve that runs to the GH 68 tank battery, which services multiple wells. A well tender noticed the GH 68 tank battery wasn't receiving as much water as they expected. CNX checked all valves in lines feeding the GH 68 tank battery. Once they located the leak at the GH122 they shut down the wells and blew down the brine line. As of 04/16/2020 CNX estimates the spill is 60% remediated. Borden indicated CNX will be remediating via alternate method and may pursue Act 2 for release of liability. CNX indicated they will provide the Department a notification within 15 days of the spill if CNX determines to utilize Act 2.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-25 to William H Brawand in Jones Twp, Elk county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: William H Brawand
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-25
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 853697
Permit API: 047-25054
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-25
Comments: While drilling on 6/24, the operator encountered fresh water. Cement returns and drill cuttings ran down the location toward a stream. The operator dug two small pits to contain this water and solids in order to prevent discharge to the stream. Some of the dirt was pushed right to the edge of the stream. Rain overnight 6/24-25 allowed the pits to overflow and also caused sediment to run into the stream from the location and dirt piles. At the time of this inspection, the stream and pits were both colored with sediment, which could also be seen in a pond just downstream. Drilling will continue 6/26-27, after which the drilling contractor will empty the pits and backfill. It was suggested that they pump the water as far from the stream as possible and/or use a sediment filter bag to prevent any further discharge.

Comments: 08/09/2023This administrative inspection is being conducted for the Ironman Well Site following violations issued on 07/18/2023 (IR: 3589336, Enf: 418538).Violations of 78a57(a), 78a66(b)1ii, 78a66(b)1i, 78a66(b)2, 91.33(A), 91.34(A), 78a54, and SWMA 301 were issued on 07/18/2023, following an incident inspection conducted in response to a spill report recieved by the Department on 07/17/2023. (c)(2)(i) Within 15 business days of the spill or release, the operator or other responsible party shall provide an initial written report that includes, to the extent that the information is available, the following:(A) The regulated substance involved.(B) The location where the spill or release occurred.(C) The environmental media affected.(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities.(F) Interim remedial actions planned, initiated or completed.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible partyintends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedulefor site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated timeframes within which it expects to take those actions.The following deficiencies were noted within the 15 Day Report submitted on 08/02/2023:(A) The regulated substance involved: EQT's report mentions leak from dump line, but does not specifically mention the regulated substance.(C) EQT's report did not mention an assessment of potential impact to Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible party intends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedule for site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated time frames within which it expects to take those actions: EQT mentions entering Act 2, but provides no timeline. EQT indicates assessment will focus on dump line trench and northern pad slope, but does not discuss WOC.Due to the deficiencies noted within the 15 Day Report, a violation of 78a66(c)2i is being issued for the failure to provide a complete initial written report within 15 days. Violations issued on 07/18/2023 remain outstanding.

On 04/15/2020 Kyle Borden of CNX reported a 5 barrel produced fluid release from a valve in a 3" produced water line servicing the GH 122 well. On 04/16/2020 I spoke to Kyle Borden via phone. Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well. This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. There are no apparent surface issues on the location location or the spur road leading to it.A tank battery located along FR 370 approximately 250 feet northwest of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks (11883 and 11884) within an earthen containment. There is evidence of repeated discharges of production water inside of the containment from each tank. Soil specific conductance (SPC) readings upwards of 15,000 uS/cm were detected at/downslope of the drains located on the back side of each tank. Elevated SPC is prevalent across the ground inside of the containment downslope of the tanks. Accumulated fluid pooled along the western wall of the containment has an SPC over 20,000 uS/cm. There was no active discharge at time of inspection.The fluids released inside of the containment have seeped through the northern corner of the earthen containment wall (or there is a buried drain) at 41.99216N / 78.76119 W. There is an approximate 25' x 3' area of stained soil with elevated SPC (upwards of 818 uS/cm vs 40 uS/cm of nearby uncontaminated soil) present outside of the containment's northern corner. The end of the apparent contaminated soil is located approximately 75 feet from Yeager Brook.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery containment to contain fluid inside of it will also nee to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/23/2025
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 8250023
Permit API: 125-29133
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 9/23/2025
Comments: On September 23, 2025, the DEP conducted an inspection at the Schwotzer Arthur well site. This inspection was conducted in response to a Post-Drilling Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) that was submitted by the operator on August 6, 2025 for well 6H (125-29133). A notarized Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration was submitted with the WSRR, as sound walls currently remain onsite. Total Depth was obtained on November 17, 2024 according to the Well Record, therefore site restoration is to be complete by August 17, 2025.An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit (ESP07632300100E) was issued by the DEP for this site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029.The following was observed:Accumulated fine sediment from the access road was observed in the rock-lined channel along Rural Valley Road (photo 3). This sedimentation has not reached the storm culvert where it empties (photo 4). No accelerated erosion rills were observed on the access road and well pad at the time of inspection (photos 2, 9, and 21). Exposed soil was observed in several areas onsite which appear to require additional temporary stabilization (photos 6 and 19). The soil crack that was present on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad appears to be repaired. Riprap has been added to this location to improve drainage (photo 12). No toe bulge was observed below at the time of inspection. Repair work has been conducted on the slough that occurred on the well pad cutslope, with no loose sediment observed in the vegetated channel below (photos 14-18). What appears to be surface cracking was observed at the top of well pad cut slope (photo 20). This appears to be due to recent excessive dryness onsite. No toe bulge was observed belowThe Act 9 sign is fully visible at the entrance of the access road, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 22). The GPU units onsite are equipped with interconnected drip pans (photo 23). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the DEP for use on 6/21/2022. Well 6H is equipped with a well tag and appears to be in production (photo 24). No evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it was observed. There are six additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Well permits, Individual E and S permit approval letter, E and S permit drawings, and E and S inspection log are onsite (photo 25). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.Based on observations from this inspection, the WSRR is denied. Because the well site is not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth, violations are being issued for failure to restore 9 months post-drilling.While the DEP was onsite, Jessica Ullom from Range Resources arrived onsite. The DEP spoke with Ullom to inform them of the forthcoming recommendations in this inspection report.The DEP recommends that the access road is maintained in a manner that prevents fine sediment from accumulating further in stormwater discharge areas, including by conducting maintenance in accordance with the access road cross section shown on page C134 of site permit plans. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further assessment and evaluation in a future follow up inspection.The DEP also recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the site and implement temporary stabilization where exposed soil is found. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further assessment and evaluation in a future follow up inspection. Finally, the DEP recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the soil cracking at the top of the well pad cutslope to determine whether it threatens site stability or is due to recent dry conditions, and that the operator notify the DEP of findings.

According to EQT, the spill occurred on November 2, 2025 when a spring on the pressure relief hose failed on a tanker truck and caused produced fluid to spill on two separate areas of the access road to the Harry Stryker Well Pad. It appeared that EQT contractors only had to scrape the surface of the impacted areas to remove the impacted soil. The contaminated soil had been hauled offsite for disposal. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 noted but were immediately corrected.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. Stressed vegetation, elevated SPC readings and abundant deer tracks are present in the ditch between the tank battery and the cross culvert and continue in a channel down to the next lease road (near 053-29533) approximately 300 feet beyond the culvert outlet.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29907, 053-29935 and 053-29916 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Comments: On 1/14/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 20 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on location. Snow was scattered across the location. While inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I met Seneca's Ian Thom who described upcoming operations as follows: A vent pipe sticking from the ground and connected to the well casing may have been jarred during construction activities, causing the well to start bubbling. A Plants and Goodwin well servicing rig is mobilizing to the site to pump cement downhole. A secondary containment structure has been installed around the wellhead and two frac tanks remain on site, staged in secondary containment.I met Seneca's Jim Westfield on the north pad who described current operations as follows: The five newly drilled and completed wells are staged for flow-back. Two sand separators were attached to each wellhead. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Six frac tanks were staged north of the wellheads for flowback operations. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads.28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. Jim was unsure if these would be left on site for the next round of drilling and completion.Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Due to frozen conditions during this inspection, conductivity readings were not taken. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. As recommended in the inspections listed above, the DEP continues to recommend pursuing Act 2 for the large amount of elevated conducted fluids discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin.The DEP recommends the following: 1. Continue to determine the cause of elevated conductance discovered during previous inspections to prevent future occurrences. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.I left the site at 1525 hours.

Comments: On April 24, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. According to the incident report that was submitted by the operator, this spill occurred on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM and resulted in an estimated 50 barrel release of production fluids to the ground. This spill report was received by the Department at 2:16 PM.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who explained that the brine tank valve failed and was ejected from the brine tank, which resulted in the release of an estimated 50 barrels of a brine and crude oil mixture. This was quantified based on the most recent fluid level measurement taken on the brine tank. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth are reported to have occurred. Penneco representative John Dohman was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Dohman who confirmed that no impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth have resulted from this incident. No identifiable water resources were visible from the location of the release. Mr. Dohman estimated that the release traveled approximately 70 yards down the slope adjacent to the brine tank and was stopped by a fallen tree. He explained that absorbent material was placed on the impacted area to absorb any standing production fluids and oil absorbent booms were placed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the release. Remediation of the impacted area is to be conducted by Moody and Associates and is scheduled to commence on the day following this inspection.The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. An area of minor staining was observed on the surface of the well site (see photo 5). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 6). The failed brine tank valve appears to have been replaced (see photos 7 and 8). No fluids were observed escaping the brine tank at the time of inspection, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased. A path of brown staining was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank (see photos 9-18). The path of travel appears to be 70 yards, per Mr. Dohman's estimate. A faint crude oil odor was detectable from the impacted area. No evidence of visual impacts was observed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the travel of the released production fluids.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery. Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned. The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

Comments: On May 12, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4179368.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 2/23/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 11/23/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plans on site have not been updated as stated in the NOV Response (IR 4166188). The plans appear to be unchanged and do not include wetland delineations in any of the drawings or added wetland seed mix(es) to Detail 06.- CFS near the access road entrance is not properly installed at this time (Photo 5).- Gravel from the RCE remains on site. The Department recommends the operator remove all gravel that is not pre-existing from the site.- A berm appears to have been constructed (Photo 7). The Department requests information regarding the purpose of the berm and if it is to remain post-restoration.- The site appears to have been seeded and mulched, with vegetation growing in some areas at this time.- What appears to be third party disturbance in the form of a two track trail is observed from the access road through site, and exiting over CFS (Photos 7-8, 11, 13, 15, 23).- CFS surrounding the site is improperly installed (Photos 11, 12, 21) including portions that have been repaired multiple times causing the sock to flatten. The Department recommends the operator replace the repaired portions of CFS.- CFS where the surface water exits the site appears to be failing, showing signs of overtopping and undercutting. The Department recommends the operator replace the current CFS and properly maintain CFS on site until restoration is achieved.- The absorbent pads that were left on site by the operator appear to remain on site at this time. The Department recommends the operator remove the absorbent pads from the site.Violations remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: Site inspection conducted on May 9, 2024 regarding a complaint called into the Department of a brine leak. During the inspection I observed a dead spot of vegetation extending approximately 55' long and approximately 16' in the widest spot. The soil was inundated with deer tracks. I used a soil Hanna Groline soil probe to screen for conductivity. All readings exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. A small drip was observed coming from the brine tank valve set area. A screw has been inserted into the brine tank to help stop the leak. Fluids still remain within the poly brine tank and the well is active. The Department recommends addressing the brine release. Violations have been cited for the brine release.Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, the chart recorder has not been changed in months. The well tag has the previous operators name and contact information listed on. The Department recommends updating the contact information.
